text: Two events have a timelike separation. According to the book, this means:
choices: ds² < 0, a massive particle can travel between them, and their time ordering is absolute
ds² > 0, no signal can connect them, and their time ordering is frame-dependent
ds² = 0, and only a light ray can connect them
ds² < 0, but the two events are causally disconnected
explanation: For timelike separation ds² < 0 (in the −+++ convention) the spatial separation is less than c times the temporal separation, so a massive particle can connect the events and all observers agree on their time ordering. Choice 1 describes spacelike separation (ds² > 0) and choice 2 describes null separation (ds² = 0). The classification is Lorentz-invariant.
